title: Identify the anchor
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What pattern from childhood shows up when you are under pressure?

There is a saying I have said before on the calls, I said: show me a successful adult and I'll show you a successful child. We have anchors in our life, emotional, physical or verbal, events that define who we are.
I asked: do we ever escape the traumas we had from our childhood and the things that define us as adults? What strategies do we have?

A student said: I wouldn't say there is a direct strategy. If you identify things from your childhood that you don't like, like chaos, and I've never known what stability is, then it's a foreign concept, and kind of a myth. Stability is not stability if anyone else can shake it.
If your idea of stability is a steady paycheck every two weeks, the student said, entrepreneurship might not be for you. You have to learn how to tame the chaos.

I have read good books on this, I said. Neurolinguistic programming is about recognizing negative anchors and positive anchors. The first thing is identification: that's not me, that's my father coming out on me, or that's a traumatic event.

I told of a business man who snapped at me, yelling, and then stopped himself: I'm sorry, that was out of place. I went bankrupt over this issue, fighting with partners. It gave me an allergy. Moments like that come up from the subconscious, I said.
We have to be aware of those negative anchors because they will get us, I said. Identify it, stop it, and say: that's not me, that's not my choice.

It is also a discipline to wake up every day inspired, I said: I'm grateful I'm alive, I'm working. Nobody wants to see the leader who is up and down in deep depressions or a bad mood. Everybody wants the leader who is inspired and looking for positive outcomes.
What is the anchor you catch in yourself, and what do you say to stop it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one habit you picked up in childhood that shows up under stress.
Write the sentence you will say to yourself: that's not me.
Write how you start the morning so you can lead.

check.q: What did I call events that define who we are?
What is the first thing, according to me, in dealing with a negative anchor?
What did a student say about stability?
choices: It is not stability if anyone else can shake it

recap: Identify your anchors. Say: that's not me. Tame the chaos.
